boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named CSUN spaces for collaborative work, quiet reading, making, recreation, wellness, and campus events.

cards.title: Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: University Library, Main Floor
cards.notes: Use the movable seating, charging points, and collaborative tables to meet classmates or settle in between classes; keep voices at a collaborative-study level.
cards.short_summary: A flexible library floor built for individual work and group collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN says the Learning Commons extends throughout the University Library's first floor and provides seating for individual reading and group collaboration.
cards.access_notes: Located in the University Library; follow current library building hours and noise policy.

cards.title: Creative Maker Studio
cards.subtitle: University Library, Main Floor West Wing
cards.notes: Reserve a workstation or service that fits your project, then use the studio's design, production, crafting, or prototyping tools with campus support.
cards.short_summary: CSUN's library makerspace for digital media, physical crafting, and creative technology.
cards.evidence_claim: The Creative Maker Studio provides currently enrolled CSUN students resources and support for learning technologies, prototyping, collaboration, and digital creation.
cards.access_notes: For currently enrolled CSUN students; located on the Main Floor West Wing and some services require reservations.

cards.title: Quiet Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: University Library, Fourth Floor East Wing
cards.notes: Bring independent reading or writing here when you need a quieter setting; choose a study pod or charger-equipped seat and observe the quiet-study rules.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor library lounge oriented toward quiet, individual focus.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN identifies the Quiet Study Lounge in the fourth-floor east wing as a quiet space with individual study pods and built-in chargers.
cards.access_notes: Fourth floor, east wing of the University Library; follow current library hours and quiet-study policy.

cards.title: Map Collection Reading Room
cards.subtitle: University Library, UL 26
cards.notes: Take the Learning Commons stairs or elevator down to browse atlases and maps, or use the open study seating when a collaborative library setting works.
cards.short_summary: An open study room beside CSUN's extensive map and atlas collection.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN describes the Map Collection Reading Room, UL 26, as an open study space available to all users with books and atlases available for browsing.
cards.access_notes: Accessible from the main-floor staircase or elevator in the Learning Commons; follow library hours.

cards.entity_name: Bob and Maureen Gohstand Leisure Reading Room
cards.title: Gohstand Leisure Reading Room
cards.subtitle: University Library, Second Floor West Wing
cards.notes: Choose this designated reading room for a calmer reading session, then return borrowed material through normal library service points when you are finished.
cards.short_summary: A named library reading room set aside specifically for reading.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN states that the Gohstand Leisure Reading Room in the second-floor west wing is a quiet space specifically designated for reading.
cards.access_notes: Second floor, west wing of the University Library; follow current library hours.

cards.title: ASRS Viewing Room
cards.subtitle: University Library, Main Floor East Wing
cards.notes: Use this named east-wing room for collaborative library work or pause to view programming on the media wall; keep audio and conversation considerate.
cards.short_summary: A main-floor viewing room and collaborative-study area near the library's automated storage system.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN's library noise policy lists the ASRS Viewing Room on the main floor as a collaborative-study location.
cards.access_notes: Main Floor East Wing of the University Library; talking is permitted at a low volume under the collaborative-study policy.

cards.title: Student Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: University Student Union
cards.notes: Plan a workout, group exercise class, or pool visit around the building schedule, and check SRC membership and program requirements before arriving.
cards.short_summary: The USU's large recreation facility for exercise, leisure, aquatics, and group classes.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN describes the Student Recreation Center as a facility for exercise and leisure activity and lists free group exercise and mindfulness classes for the CSUN community.
cards.access_notes: Current fall/spring building hours listed by CSUN are Monday-Friday 6 a.m.-10 p.m. and weekends 9 a.m.-5 p.m.; eligibility may apply.

cards.title: Oasis Wellness Center
cards.subtitle: University Student Union
cards.notes: Use the wellness center's relaxation and contemplation areas as intended, and check the SRC schedule or reservation process before planning a program or room use.
cards.short_summary: A USU wellness destination with indoor relaxation areas and an outdoor labyrinth.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN's Oasis opening announcement describes relaxation rooms, power-napping sleep pods, outdoor lounges and contemplation areas including the Oasis Labyrinth.
cards.source_title: New Oasis Wellness Center Opening Aug. 24 for all CSUN Students
cards.access_notes: The Oasis is in USU Building E; CSUN directs visitors to SRC hours and USU reservations for operations and reservable use.

cards.title: Games Room
cards.subtitle: University Student Union, East Conference Center
cards.notes: Coordinate a low-key game session with friends, then check the USU schedule and reservation rules before relying on the room for an organized activity.
cards.short_summary: A named USU recreation room for billiards and PC or console gaming.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN's Student Recreation Center page invites visitors to the Games Room for billiards and current PC and console games.
cards.access_notes: CSUN lists the Games Room in the USU East Conference Center; reservations may be required for group use.

cards.title: Plaza del Sol
cards.subtitle: University Student Union
cards.notes: Check the USU calendar for performances, meetings, or campus events here, and use the space according to any posted event or reservation instructions.
cards.short_summary: A named University Student Union venue for small, medium, and large events.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN's properties listing identifies Plaza del Sol as a University Student Union venue for small-, medium-, and large-scale events.
cards.access_notes: CSUN lists Plaza del Sol as public with limited access; current listed USU hours are Monday-Thursday 7 a.m.-10 p.m., Friday 7 a.m.-7 p.m., and weekends 8 a.m.-5 p.m.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission activities and spaces at CSUN, with access limits noted where they apply.

cards.title: Browse the Main Gallery
cards.subtitle: Art & Design Center
cards.notes: Meet at the Art & Design Center and take in the current large-scale exhibition. Confirm the posted schedule before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission campus art stop with professional and student exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN states that admission to all Art Galleries spaces and programs is free for everyone; the Main Gallery is in the Art & Design Center.
cards.source_title: Current Art & Events | CSUN Art Galleries
cards.access_notes: Free admission. Posted hours are Monday–Thursday; Friday and Saturday visits are by appointment.

cards.title: See a West Gallery exhibition
cards.subtitle: Art & Design Center
cards.notes: Use the West Gallery for a short art-focused meetup, then discuss the show outside the gallery rather than rushing through it.
cards.short_summary: A compact interdisciplinary exhibition space on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN identifies the West Gallery as an Art & Design Center gallery and states that admission to all Art Galleries spaces and programs is free for everyone.
cards.source_title: Current Art & Events | CSUN Art Galleries
cards.access_notes: Free admission. Check the gallery’s posted hours and exhibition schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Visit Manzanita Gallery
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Manzanita Hall
cards.notes: Head to the second floor of Manzanita Hall to view student-club-organized work, and allow time to read the exhibition materials.
cards.short_summary: A satellite gallery where CSUN student clubs organize exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN lists Manzanita Gallery on the second floor of Manzanita Hall and states that admission to all Art Galleries spaces and programs is free for everyone.
cards.source_title: Current Art & Events | CSUN Art Galleries
cards.access_notes: Free admission. Check the gallery’s posted hours and whether an exhibition is installed.

cards.title: Catch a Cinematheque screening
cards.subtitle: Elaine and Alan Armer Screening Room, Manzanita Hall 100
cards.notes: Choose a listing from the public screening schedule and arrive early with a friend; the program notes that seating is limited.
cards.short_summary: Year-round campus film screenings, often paired with a lecture or Q&A.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN describes the Cinematheque’s Armer Theater public screenings as free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public; use the public screening schedule and arrive early because seating may be limited.

cards.title: Arrange a Botanic Garden tour
cards.subtitle: CSUN Botanic Garden
cards.notes: If you are organizing a local K–12 or college group, contact the garden at least four weeks ahead to request a guided visit.
cards.short_summary: A guided academic-garden activity for eligible local school and college groups.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN says its Botanic Garden tours for local K–12 and college schools are free of charge and should be arranged at least four weeks in advance.
cards.access_notes: Free only for local K–12 and college school groups; advance arrangements are required.

cards.title: Use a visitor computer
cards.subtitle: University Library Learning Commons
cards.notes: Bring a valid photo ID, ask Library Technology Services for a station, and use the two-hour session to research or work together.
cards.short_summary: A first-come public computer option in the Learning Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN provides visitor computer stations for community use; non-CSUN visitors may request a two-hour session with valid picture ID.
cards.source_title: Visitor Computer Access | CSUN University Library
cards.access_notes: No purchase is required. Visitors need valid photo ID; stations are first-come and campus users receive priority.

cards.title: Scan notes or finds together
cards.subtitle: University Library Learning Commons
cards.notes: Bring your own material or locate a non-circulating item, then use the free public scanners to save or email a shared reference copy.
cards.short_summary: A practical no-cost library activity for saving documents digitally.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN states that visitors without a Library card and users of non-circulating materials may use the Library’s free public scanners.
cards.access_notes: Free public scanners are available, with campus users and government-document users prioritized during busy times.

cards.title: Explore government publications
cards.subtitle: CSUN University Library
cards.notes: Pick a local, state, or federal topic and use the library’s government publications access to compare sources and save useful documents.
cards.short_summary: A public-research hang built around government information.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN states that free public access to government publications is ensured by law and that free reference assistance and scanning or saving are available to any library user.
cards.access_notes: Free public access applies to government publications; ask library staff for help locating material.

cards.title: Browse CSUN ScholarWorks
cards.subtitle: Online CSUN institutional repository
cards.notes: Search for a topic, creator, or department, then trade links to an openly accessible paper or project for a low-key online study break.
cards.short_summary: An online repository for freely accessible CSUN scholarship.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN’s ScholarWorks policy states that full-text items in externally accessible repository areas are available free of charge.
cards.source_title: CSUN Oviatt Library Self-Archiving and Repository Policy
cards.access_notes: Use externally accessible repository items; access is online and no purchase or admission is required.

cards.title: Listen to KCSN together
cards.subtitle: CSUN public radio, online
cards.notes: Put on KCSN’s web stream while you work, draw, or cook at home, and use the station’s playlist as a shared listening prompt.
cards.short_summary: CSUN’s public-radio stream can be listened to online without fees.
cards.evidence_claim: The Daily Sundial reported that KCSN streams its music online with no fees.
cards.source_title: Westfield Topanga prepares for grand opening for new KCSN station | Daily Sundial
cards.access_notes: The station’s online stream was reported as having no fees; internet access is required.
